title: Nommer les animaux, les femelles et les petits
summary: Learn common animal families with articles and distinguish grammatical gender from biological sex.
objectives: Name common domestic males, females and young animals.
Use each noun's article and agreement correctly.
Avoid assuming every animal name forms a feminine or young form regularly.

sources.label: B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: Some related words change predictably, others do not
paragraphs: Learn an animal noun with its article, not as an isolated English translation. Un chien (masculine) is a dog or male dog; une chienne (feminine) is a female dog; un chiot (masculine) is a puppy. Un chat (masculine) is a cat or male cat; une chatte (feminine) is a female cat; un chaton (masculine) is a kitten. Un lapin (masculine), une lapine (feminine) and un lapereau (masculine) are a rabbit/male rabbit, female rabbit and young rabbit.

A masculine family or species word can be used when sex is unknown or irrelevant. A grammatical gender is not a biological claim: un chaton femelle is a female kitten, but chaton remains grammatically masculine. The noun's gender controls adjectives; mâle and femelle can specify sex without changing that noun.
points: Plural forms are ordinary here: chiens, chiennes, chiots; chats, chattes, chatons; lapins, lapines, lapereaux.
Lapereau has plural lapereaux, like many nouns ending in -eau.

examples.english: The female dog accompanies her two puppies.
examples.note: Chienne is feminine; chiots is masculine plural.

examples.english: This female kitten is very curious.
examples.note: Chaton stays masculine even when its sex is specified.

examples.english: The female rabbit stays near the young rabbits.
examples.note: The young animal has a distinct noun, not a regular suffix added in the sentence.

mistakes.why: For the female cat as mother, use the feminine noun chatte with la.

sections.title: Farm animal families often need different roots
paragraphs: Horse: un cheval (masculine), horse; un étalon (masculine), a breeding stallion; une jument (feminine), mare; un poulain (masculine), foal or male foal; une pouliche (feminine), female foal. Cattle: un taureau (masculine), bull; une vache (feminine), cow; un veau (masculine), calf. Un bœuf (masculine) is an ox/castrated male, not the ordinary word for any bull.

Sheep: un bélier (masculine), ram; une brebis (feminine), ewe; un agneau (masculine), lamb; une agnelle (feminine), female lamb. Un mouton (masculine) can name a sheep generically and can also designate a castrated male. Goats: un bouc (masculine), male goat; une chèvre (feminine), female goat or generic goat in ordinary contexts; un chevreau (masculine), kid.

Pigs: un porc or un cochon (masculine), pig; un verrat (masculine), breeding male pig; une truie (feminine), sow; un porcelet (masculine), piglet. Donkeys: un âne (masculine), donkey or male donkey; une ânesse (feminine), female donkey; un ânon (masculine), young donkey. Do not replace every generic name with a specialist sex term unless the distinction matters.
points: Useful irregular plurals: chevaux, taureaux, veaux, agneaux, chevreaux; brebis keeps its written s in singular and plural.
An ordinary descriptive fallback such as un veau femelle can be clearer for a learner than an unfamiliar specialist age term.

examples.english: The mare walks with her foal.
examples.note: Horse and mare use different roots.

examples.french: Les **vaches** et les **veaux** sont dans le pré.
examples.english: The cows and calves are in the field.
examples.note: Veau becomes veaux in the plural.

examples.english: A ewe watches over two lambs.
examples.note: Brebis is singular despite its final s.
Here chèvre identifies the female parent.

examples.english: The sow rests near the piglets.
examples.note: The female pig has a distinct name.

mistakes.avoid: Une cheval attend près de la barrière.
mistakes.prefer: Une jument attend près de la barrière.
mistakes.why: For a specifically female adult horse, use une jument. Cheval itself is grammatically masculine.

sections.title: Bird families and safe general descriptions
paragraphs: Chickens: un coq (masculine), rooster; une poule (feminine), hen; un poussin (masculine), chick. Ducks: un canard (masculine), duck or male duck; une cane (feminine), female duck; un caneton (masculine), duckling. Geese: un jars (masculine), gander; une oie (feminine), goose; un oison (masculine), gosling. Turkeys: un dindon (masculine), male turkey; une dinde (feminine), female turkey; un dindonneau (masculine), young turkey.

Some species names have only one usual grammatical gender regardless of sex: une souris (feminine), a mouse, can refer to a male or female animal. Une souris mâle remains feminine for agreement. When a precise young-animal word is unknown, un petit or les petits in an established animal context often works; do not manufacture a new feminine or baby form.
points: Poussin is a young bird word especially associated with chickens; it does not mean an adult small hen.
Cane has one n; canne with two n is a different noun meaning a walking stick or cane.

examples.english: A female duck swims ahead of three ducklings.
examples.note: Cane is the female duck, not canne.

sections.title: Nommer l'espèce sans inventer le sexe
paragraphs: Two useful wildlife families are un lion (masculine), lion; une lionne (feminine), lioness; un lionceau (masculine), lion cub; and un cerf (masculine), stag or deer of the species; une biche (feminine), doe; un faon (masculine), fawn. Do not assume that a young animal is male just because its ordinary noun is masculine. Un lionceau femelle and un faon femelle retain masculine grammatical agreement.

For a wildlife observation, first decide what is actually known: species, age and sex are separate pieces of information. Use the sex-specific word when that distinction is supported by the context; otherwise a species or young-animal term can be enough. The plural lionceaux follows the -eau pattern already used for other young animals.
points: These are recognition and description terms, not a requirement to memorize every zoological age label.

examples.french: La caméra a filmé une **biche** avec son **faon**.
examples.english: The camera filmed a doe with her fawn.
examples.note: The nouns distinguish an adult female from a young animal; faon alone does not specify the young animal's sex.

examples.french: La fiche indique : « Un **lionceau femelle**, encore très **jeune**. »
examples.english: The record says: 'A female lion cub, still very young.'
examples.note: Femelle adds biological information without replacing the masculine article un.

examples.english: The lion cubs stay near the lioness.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a female dog, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: The female noun is chienne, feminine.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a kitten, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Chaton is grammatically masculine.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a mare, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: An adult female horse is une jument.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a chick, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: A chick is un poussin.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a calf, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Veau is the young animal in the cattle family.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a ewe, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Brebis is feminine and already ends in s.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a male goat, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Bouc names the male goat.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a sow, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Truie is the female pig.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a female duck using its specific sex term, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Cane has one n.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a rooster, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Coq is the adult male chicken.

practice.prompt: Supply curieux in the correct form: Ce chaton femelle est ___.
practice.explanation: The noun chaton is grammatically masculine despite biological sex.

practice.prompt: Give the plural of un agneau, including the plural indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Agneau has plural agneaux.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a female donkey, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: The feminine donkey noun is ânesse.

practice.prompt: Give the French noun phrase for a gosling, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Oison is the young animal in the goose family.

practice.prompt: Supply petit in the correct form: Cette souris mâle est ___.
practice.explanation: Souris remains grammatically feminine.

practice.prompt: Choose the accurate distinction.
choices: Un taureau is a bull; un bœuf is an ox/castrated male.
Un bœuf is the standard female counterpart of un taureau.
answers: Un taureau is a bull; un bœuf is an ox/castrated male.
practice.explanation: The female counterpart is une vache; bœuf does not mean cow.

practice.prompt: Give the taught noun for a puppy, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Chiot names the young dog and is grammatically masculine.

practice.prompt: Give the specific noun phrase for an adult female cat, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: The feminine adult noun is chatte.

practice.prompt: Give the three taught rabbit-family terms in male/female/young order, each with an indefinite article. Join all three noun phrases with et, without commas.
answers: un lapin et une lapine et un lapereau
practice.explanation: Lapin/lapine distinguish adults; lapereau names the young animal.

practice.prompt: Give the specific adult goose terms in male/female order, each with an indefinite article. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: The male and female use distinct words: jars and oie.

practice.prompt: Give the three taught turkey-family terms in male/female/young order, each with an indefinite article. Join all three noun phrases with et, without commas.
answers: un dindon et une dinde et un dindonneau
practice.explanation: Dindon and dinde name the adults; dindonneau names the young.

practice.prompt: Give the taught terms for a breeding stallion and a female foal, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: Étalon specifies a breeding male; pouliche specifies a young female.

practice.prompt: Give the specific terms for a ram and a female lamb, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: Bélier is the adult male sheep; agnelle is a female lamb.

practice.prompt: Give the taught terms for a female goat and a kid, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: The female parent is une chèvre; the young animal is un chevreau.

practice.prompt: Give the terms for a breeding male pig and a piglet, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: Verrat is more specific than the generic porc/cochon; porcelet names the young.

practice.prompt: Give the taught terms for an adult male donkey and a young donkey, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: Âne and ânon are masculine and both retain the circumflex.

practice.prompt: Give the specific adult female counterpart of un taureau, with the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: The female is une vache, not un bœuf.

practice.prompt: Give the ordinary plural of un cheval, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Cheval has the irregular plural chevaux.

practice.prompt: Give the taught generic sheep term, not the specific ram or ewe term, with an indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Mouton can name the animal generically when sex is not the point.

practice.prompt: Give the ordinary male/generic adult terms for dog and cat, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: These masculine nouns can also name the animals when sex is unknown or irrelevant.

practice.prompt: Give the taught male/generic adult duck term and the duckling term, in that order, with indefinite articles. Join the two noun phrases with et.
practice.explanation: Canard names the adult; caneton names the young.

practice.prompt: Give the specific adult female counterpart of un coq, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: The adult female chicken is une poule.

practice.prompt: Give either of the two taught generic adult words for a pig, including an indefinite article. Do not use the specialist breeding-male term.
practice.explanation: Porc and cochon are both taught generic terms; verrat is more specific.

practice.prompt: Give the plural of un lapereau, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: The young-rabbit noun takes the regular -eau to -eaux plural.

practice.prompt: Give the taught masculine noun for a foal, including the indefinite article.
practice.explanation: Poulain can be the generic foal term or specify a male foal; pouliche specifies a female.

practice.prompt: A wildlife caption must name an adult female deer and a fawn. Give the two specific taught noun phrases in that order, each with an indefinite article, joined with et.
practice.explanation: Biche identifies the adult female; faon identifies a young deer without necessarily specifying its sex.

practice.prompt: Pluralize only the noun in un lionceau to label several cubs. Give the plural noun without an article.
practice.explanation: Lionceau takes -eaux in the plural, like veau and lapereau.

practice.prompt: Agree blessé with the grammatical noun, not the animal's sex: Le faon femelle est ___.
practice.explanation: Faon is masculine even when femelle specifies the animal's sex.

production_task.prompt: Write a short description for visitors to a small educational farm. Mention three adult/young animal families and include one sentence where grammatical gender stays fixed despite the animal's sex.
production_task.model_answer: Près de l'entrée, la jument marche avec son poulain. Les vaches restent à l'ombre avec les veaux. Une poule guide ses poussins vers l'abri. Dans la maison, un chaton femelle très curieux observe les visiteurs.
production_task.translation: Near the entrance, the mare walks with her foal. The cows stay in the shade with the calves. A hen leads her chicks towards the shelter. In the house, a very curious female kitten watches the visitors.
rubric: Use articles and genders for the animal nouns.
Distinguish adult, female and young terms where the description requires it.
Keep adjective agreement tied to grammatical gender.
Avoid inventing forms by adding e or a guessed baby suffix.
